records.analysis: Private authoring context: the fix restricts Sequence case conversion to ASCII letters. Before it, Sequence.lowercase() XOR-ed the case bit 0x20 into every byte selected by the lowercase mask, and the constructor's lowercase handling classified every byte greater than 'Z' (90) as lowercase and toggled it. The commit message documents the corruption: gaps, dots and stop codons became control characters ('-' to carriage return, '.' to 0x0e, '*' to newline) and lowercase letters were uppercased; punctuation above 'Z' (brackets, caret, underscore, backtick, braces, pipe, tilde, backslash) was rewritten in generic Sequence objects (e.g. '_' became DEL) and flagged as lowercase. The FASTA/FASTQ writers forward their lowercase option to Sequence.lowercase(), so such masks silently corrupted written files. Test evidence: before the fix 4 tests failed (316 passed); after, all 320 pass. (1) FASTA writer, DNA 'ACGT-NNAC' with a lowercase mask over positions 2-5: the gap was written as a carriage return; expected '>s1<n>ACgt-nNAC<n>'. (2) FASTQ writer, same input: expected '@s1<n>ACgt-nNAC<n>+<n>?????????<n>', gap written as a carriage return. (3) Sequence('AC-GT.N*_[~]acgt').lowercase with an all-True mask returned 'ac<CR>gt<0x0e>n<LF><DEL>{^}ACGT' instead of 'ac-gt.n*_[~]acgt'. (4) Sequence('ac_g[t]{n}~`^|<backslash>', lowercase='lc') became 'AC<DEL>G{T}[N]^@~<backslash>|' with all 15 positions flagged lowercase, instead of 'AC_G[T]{N}~`^|<backslash>' with only a, c, g, t, n flagged. Caveat: the captured FASTA/FASTQ failure lines render the corrupted sequence as 'ACgt<CR>d NAC'; the 'd ' is a logging artifact around a carriage-return escape followed by 'nNAC' — the actual written sequence is 'ACgt' + carriage return + 'nNAC', consistent with the '-' to carriage-return mapping (the Sequence-level failure is clean and confirms the byte mappings). Root cause: case conversion is applied unconditionally instead of being restricted to ASCII letters; XOR 0x20 maps '-' (0x2D) to CR (0x0D), '.' (0x2E) to 0x0E, '*' (0x2A) to LF (0x0A), '_' (0x5F) to DEL (0x7F), '[' to '{', ']' to '}', '^' to '~', backtick to '@', '|' to backslash, and uppercases a-z; the constructor likewise rewrites and misflags every character above 'Z' that is not a lowercase letter. Expected: lowercase() converts only A-Z at selected positions, leaving all other selected characters (including already-lowercase letters) unchanged; the constructor's lowercase parameter treats only a-z as lowercase; the writers emit masked non-letters unchanged. Issue strategy: user-discovered bug report with three short reproduction scripts (lowercase() on a mixed-character Sequence, the FASTA writer showing file corruption, the constructor with lowercase='lc'), verbatim corrupted outputs and explicit expected outputs; no test names, files, commit/PR references, or implementation prescriptions.
records.instruction: The developer must fix Sequence's case conversion so that it only affects ASCII letters. Specifically: (1) Sequence.lowercase() must convert only uppercase letters A-Z at the positions selected by its lowercase argument to lowercase; every other character at those positions (gaps '-', dots '.', stop codons '*', brackets, and characters already lowercase) must be returned unchanged instead of having its case bit flipped into control characters or wrong symbols. (2) The lowercase constructor parameter (True or a metadata key) must recognize only a-z as lowercase: those characters are uppercased and flagged in the positional metadata, while any other character above 'Z' (brackets, underscore, backtick, braces, pipe, tilde, backslash, caret) must be stored as-is and not flagged. (3) As a consequence, the FASTA and FASTQ writers' lowercase option must write masked non-letter characters (gaps, degenerate characters, stop codons) unchanged instead of corrupting output files. The user-facing report below describes the bug and the expected behavior.
